subject: science
promptStrong: Give me a challenging KS3 exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for KS3 simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake.
learningObjectives: The difference between atoms, elements and compounds
Conservation of mass in chemical reactions

questions.q: In the simple (Dalton) model of the atom, an atom is described as a…
questions.explain: Dalton pictured atoms as tiny, solid spheres that cannot be created, destroyed or broken down. Smaller parts inside the atom were discovered much later.

questions.q: According to Dalton's model, which statement about atoms is correct?
options: Atoms can be created during a reaction
Atoms can be destroyed during a reaction
Atoms cannot be created or destroyed
questions.explain: A key idea of the Dalton model is that atoms cannot be created or destroyed — they are only rearranged. This underpins conservation of mass.

questions.lo: The difference between atoms, elements and compounds
options: A substance made of only one type of atom
Any substance that is a gas
A jumble of substances that are not bonded
questions.explain: An element contains only one type of atom and cannot be broken down chemically. Examples include oxygen, carbon and iron.

questions.lo: The difference between atoms, elements and compounds
options: One type of atom on its own
Two or more different atoms chemically bonded together
A single atom that has split apart
questions.explain: A compound forms when two or more different types of atom are chemically bonded. A chemical reaction is needed to make it or to split it back up.

questions.lo: The difference between atoms, elements and compounds
questions.q: Water (H₂O) is made of hydrogen and oxygen atoms bonded together. What type of substance is it?
questions.explain: Water contains two different types of atom (hydrogen and oxygen) chemically bonded, so it is a compound.

questions.lo: The difference between atoms, elements and compounds
questions.q: Which of these is an element?
questions.explain: Copper is made of only copper atoms, so it is an element. Water, carbon dioxide and salt each contain more than one type of atom bonded together, so they are compounds.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a compound and a mixture?
options: A compound has bonded atoms; a mixture is not bonded
A mixture has bonded atoms; a compound is not bonded
A compound is always a metal
questions.explain: In a compound the atoms are chemically bonded and can only be split by a reaction. In a mixture the substances are just jumbled together and can be separated physically.

questions.q: Which of these is a mixture?
questions.explain: Air is a mixture of gases (mainly nitrogen and oxygen) that are not chemically bonded, so it can be separated physically. The others are compounds.

questions.q: Sand and iron filings are stirred together but not bonded. How could you separate them, and what does this tell you?
options: A reaction is needed, so it is a compound
A magnet can pull out the iron, so it is a mixture
It cannot be separated, so it is an element
Only heating can separate it, so it is a single atom
questions.explain: Because nothing is bonded, the parts of a mixture keep their own properties and can be separated physically — here a magnet removes the iron filings. That confirms it is a mixture, not a compound.

questions.q: What is the chemical symbol for oxygen?
questions.explain: Oxygen's symbol is a single capital letter O. Chemical symbols are a worldwide code, one or two letters long.

questions.q: Which is the correctly written symbol for the element sodium?
questions.explain: Sodium's symbol is Na. The first letter is always a capital and the second is always lowercase, so only 'Na' is correct.

questions.q: Why does the symbol 'Co' mean something different from 'CO'?
options: They mean exactly the same thing
'Co' is the element cobalt; 'CO' is carbon bonded to oxygen
'Co' is a mixture and 'CO' is an element
Capital letters do not matter in chemistry
questions.explain: Capitalisation matters. 'Co' (capital then lowercase) is the single element cobalt, while 'CO' (two capitals) means one carbon atom and one oxygen atom — a compound.

questions.q: In the formula H₂O, what does the small '2' tell you?
options: The compound is 2 times heavier than normal
questions.explain: The subscript number applies to the symbol just before it, so the 2 means there are 2 hydrogen atoms. With no number after O, there is just 1 oxygen atom.

questions.q: How many atoms in total are in one unit of carbon dioxide, CO₂?
questions.explain: CO₂ has 1 carbon atom plus 2 oxygen atoms, giving 1 + 2 = 3 atoms in total.

questions.q: The formula for sulfuric acid is H₂SO₄. How many atoms are there in total in one unit?
questions.explain: Count each: 2 hydrogen + 1 sulfur + 4 oxygen = 7 atoms in total.

questions.lo: Conservation of mass in chemical reactions
questions.q: During a chemical reaction, what happens to the atoms of the reactants?
options: They are destroyed and new ones created
They are rearranged into new substances
They stop existing and reform as energy
questions.explain: In a reaction the old bonds break and new bonds form, so the same atoms are simply rearranged into new substances. No atoms are created or destroyed.

questions.lo: Conservation of mass in chemical reactions
questions.q: Which statement describes the conservation of mass?
options: Products always weigh more than reactants
Reactants always weigh more than products
The total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products
Mass is lost as gas escapes in every reaction
questions.explain: Because the same atoms are present before and after, the total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products.

questions.lo: Conservation of mass in chemical reactions
questions.q: 24 g of magnesium reacts completely with 16 g of oxygen to make magnesium oxide. What is the mass of magnesium oxide formed?
questions.explain: Mass is conserved, so mass of product = mass of reactants = 24 + 16 = 40 g.

questions.lo: Conservation of mass in chemical reactions
questions.q: In the equation CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O, there is 1 carbon, 4 hydrogen and 4 oxygen on the left. Why must the right-hand side have exactly the same?
options: Because atoms are rearranged, not created or destroyed
Because the arrow makes new atoms appear
Because gases always double the atoms
Because water is heavier than methane
questions.explain: A balanced equation must have the same number of each type of atom on both sides, because a reaction only rearranges atoms — none are created or destroyed. This is why mass is conserved.

specSource: National Curriculum in England: science programme of study, Key Stage 3; Chemistry — Atoms, elements and compounds
